caseno: Income Tax Reference Application No. 90 of 2003.
lawyer:
ABM Fazlur Rashid -----For the Applicant 
Abdur Rahim Bhuiyan, DAG with Mafuza Begum AAG ----- For the Respondent
parties:
Grameen Telecom ----- Applicant
Vs.
Commissioner of Taxes ----- Respondent
full_judgment:
"Section 28 of the said Act provides the limitation for execution case under the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and the maximum period of limitation is 6 years provided such execution case filed within one year from the disposal of the previous execution case filed under the said Act. In the instant case the provision of section 28 cannot be applied inasmuch as the limitation of 6 years expired prior to promulgation of new Act, 2003." 

 It is evident from the materials on record that the Artha Rin Suit was filed on 26-9-90 and decreed on 6-1-1992 when the Ain, 1990 was in operation. Under the Ain, 1990 the provisions of the Code were mostly applicable including the provision 48 of the Code and therefore, the decree-holder-Bank was legally entitled to file a fresh execution case within 12 years from the decree under section 48 of the code subject to the provision of Article 182 of the Limitation Act. The first execution case was dismissed on 29-4-2003 and the Ain came into operation on 1-5-2003 i.e. on the next date. The plaintiff-decree- holder Bank filed the second execution case i.e. Artha Jari Case No.22 of 2003 on 26-8- 2003 on 26-8-2003 which is within 3 years/ one year as required under Article 182 of the Limitation Act and section 28(3) of the Ain, 2003 . The decree having been passed on 6-1-1992 and the second execution case having been filed on 26-8-2003 i.e. within 12 years from the date of judgment and decree as required under section 48 of the Code and within one year as required under section 28(3) of the Ain, 2003 it cannot be treated as barred by limitation. Retrospective effect was not given to section 28(4) of the Ain, 2003 and so, there is no scope to count the period of limitation before the provision of section 28(4) of the Ain, 2003 came into operation. 

 The question raised in this writ petition about the limitation came up for consideration before the High Court Division and this Division by judgment dated 13-5-2010 passed in Writ Petition No.4723 of 2009 (Md. Yasin Miah and others vs Bangladesh and others), in which of us was a party, decided as under:- 

 "We have already noticed that the 1st execution case was filed on 14-3-2001 when the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 (the Ain, 1990, in brief) was in force and during existence of the Ain, 1990 the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure (the Code) was applicable relating to limitation in an execution case. According to the provision of section 48 of the Code an application to execute a decree is to be filed within a period of 12 years and not after and this provision was applicable at the time of filing of 1st execution case on 14- 3-2001. Later on, during pendency of the 1st execution case, the Ain, 2003 came into a play on 1st May, 2003 and' in that view of the matter, there is no scope to give retrospective effect of the provision of section 28(4) of the Ain, 2003 so to apply the period of limitation in the 2nd execution case from 14-3-2001 inasmuch as the Ain, 2003 itself was not in existence on the date of filing of the 1st execution case. The provision of section 28(4) of the Ain 2003 cannot be interpreted in such a way that section 28(4) of the Ain, 2003 can be applied from that date of institution of the 1st execution case which was filed on 14-3-2001 long before promulgation of the Ain, 2003 (1st May, 2003). We have carefully gone through the decisions as referred to by Mr. Sharif and we find that the facts and circumstance of those cases are completely different from the facts of the present case as in the cited case the execution case was filed beyond the period of 12 years. Therefore, the execution case was also barred by limitation in view of the provision of section 48 of the Code. The Judgment dated 20- 4-2009 passed by our Apex Court, in the Civil Petition for Leave To Appeal No.2 180 of2008 rather supports our view inasmuch as it has been observed in this judgment as under:- 

 In the instant case the provision of the section 28 cannot be applied inasmuch as the limitation of 6 years expired prior to promulgation of the new Act, 2003 ... " The same principle is' also applicable in this case which means that section 28(4) of the Ain, 2003 cannot be applied before promulgation Of the Ain,2003.
